about.title: Personal Injury Help in Cupertino, California
about.longDescription: Cupertino may be known for its tech campuses and quiet neighborhoods, but its roads see real traffic every day. In the most recent full year on record, Cupertino logged 160 injury collisions, resulting in 208 people hurt and 2 lives lost. Corridors like I-280, De Anza Boulevard, Stevens Creek Boulevard, and SR-85 carry heavy volume, and public crash records show these are the routes where incidents are most often reported. If you were hurt in a wreck anywhere in Cupertino, the days and weeks afterward can feel overwhelming — medical appointments, insurance calls, missed work. LawProactive is a free service that connects injured people with an independent personal injury attorney; we are not a law firm, and we don't charge you anything to make that connection. Attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover compensation. Our goal is simple: help you find someone who can explain your options under California law, without adding to your stress. You focus on healing; let us help you find the right person to talk to about what happened.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Soon

items.title: The Clock Is Running
items.desc: California generally gives you 2 years from the date of injury to file a claim, but that window shrinks to as little as 6 months if a government entity is involved. Waiting too long can cost you your right to recover anything.

items.title: Fault Doesn't Have to Be All-or-Nothing
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, meaning even if you were partly responsible for the crash, you can still recover damages — just reduced by your share of fault.

items.title: No Limit on Pain and Suffering
items.desc: Unlike some states, California places no cap on non-economic damages like pain and suffering in ordinary injury cases, so your compensation isn't artificially limited.

items.title: You Pay Nothing Upfront
items.desc: Attorneys in our network work on contingency, which means they only get paid if you win your case. There's no bill just for asking questions.

items.question: How long do I have to file a personal injury claim in Cupertino?
items.answer: California law generally allows 2 years from the date of the injury to file a claim. If a government agency or vehicle is involved, that window can shrink to as little as 6 months, so it's worth checking your situation sooner rather than later.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for the accident?
items.answer: California uses a pure comparative fault rule, which means you can still recover compensation even if you share some blame. Your total recovery is simply reduced by your percentage of fault.

items.question: Where do crashes tend to cluster in Cupertino?
items.answer: Public crash records show that corridors like I-280, De Anza Boulevard, Stevens Creek Boulevard, and SR-85 carry higher collision counts, with reports peaking on Tuesdays between 3 and 5 p.m. These are neutral, publicly reported figures, not a judgment about any particular road.

items.question: Does it cost anything to talk to an attorney through LawProactive?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service that connects you with an independent attorney, and we are not a law firm ourselves. Attorneys in our network work on contingency, so there's no fee unless you actually recover money.

items.question: Is there a cap on how much I can recover for pain and suffering?
items.answer: In ordinary personal injury cases, California does not cap non-economic damages such as pain and suffering. This is different from some other states, and an attorney can explain how it might apply to your specific situation.
